# Reseed Control Module Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The reseed control module obtains entropy reseed values for the key manager. It requests entropy from the entropy distribution network, collects enough entropy chunks to form a complete seed, and makes that seed available with a completion indication.

After the first reseed completes, the module also supports autonomous, periodic reseeding using a software-configurable interval. The first reseed must be explicitly requested; periodic reseeding is not enabled until that first operation has completed.

## 2. Reset and Initial State

After reset:

- The module shall be idle.
- It shall not issue an entropy request.
- It shall not assert a reseed completion or seed-enable indication.
- It shall not acknowledge an external reseed request.
- All counters and interval tracking state shall be cleared.
- The automatic periodic reseed path shall be disabled until the first reseed operation completes.

## 3. Reseed Triggering

A reseed operation shall start when any of the following occurs:

- An external reseed request is asserted.
- After the first reseed has completed, the interval count reaches the configured reseed interval.

The module shall allow only one reseed operation to be outstanding at a time. If a trigger arrives while a reseed operation is already in progress, it shall not start a second operation.

The external reseed request shall be treated as a level-sensitive request. The requester must keep it asserted until the module returns the completion acknowledge for that request. If an external request is asserted while a reseed is already in progress, the module may use the completion of that in-progress reseed to acknowledge the external request, provided the request is still asserted when the reseed completes.

The module shall assert the external reseed completion acknowledge only when an external request is asserted at the time a reseed operation completes. It shall not assert this acknowledge for an internally triggered periodic reseed unless an external request is also active.

## 4. Entropy Collection

Each reseed operation shall collect a fixed number of entropy chunks. The number of chunks is determined by the full seed width divided by the entropy chunk width. The module shall support configurations in which the seed width is an integer multiple of the entropy chunk width.

During a reseed operation:

- The module shall request entropy from the entropy distribution network.
- Each recognized request/acknowledge exchange on the entropy interface shall count as one received entropy chunk.
- The module shall retain all received chunks until the reseed operation completes.
- The operation shall not complete until the required number of chunks has been received.

When more than one chunk is required, the module shall form the full seed by concatenating the chunks in the order they are received. The first received chunk shall occupy the most significant portion, and the last received chunk shall occupy the least significant portion.

When the final chunk has been received:

- The reseed operation shall complete.
- The module shall assert the seed-enable indication.
- The seed output shall be valid only while seed-enable is asserted.
- Counters used for the operation shall be cleared.
- The pending entropy request state shall be released so a future reseed operation can begin.

## 5. Periodic Reseeding and Interval Counting

The module shall maintain a reseed interval count. This count shall operate only after the first reseed has completed.

Before the first reseed completion:

- The interval count shall be disabled.
- No interval-based reseed request shall be generated.
- Only an external request can start the first reseed operation.

After the first reseed completes:

- The interval count shall start from zero.
- It shall increment once per local clock cycle while no reseed operation is outstanding.
- It shall stop incrementing while a reseed operation is pending.
- It shall be cleared when a reseed operation completes.

When the interval count reaches the configured reseed interval, the module shall start a reseed operation. If the interval is changed while a reseed is already pending, the pending reseed shall continue normally, and the new interval value shall take effect for later comparisons.

A configured interval value of zero shall cause a new reseed to be requested immediately after periodic reseeding is enabled and again after each subsequent reseed completes.

## 6. Seed Output Behavior

The seed output shall be considered meaningful only when the seed-enable output is asserted. The seed-enable output shall be asserted for each completed reseed operation, including both externally requested and periodically triggered operations.

At the same time seed-enable is asserted, the seed output shall contain the complete reseed value assembled from the entropy chunks collected during that operation.

The seed-enable indication is a completion qualifier. It shall not be asserted at any other time.

## 7. Error Reporting

The module shall monitor the reseed interval counter for internal inconsistency. If an inconsistency is detected, the module shall assert the counter error output.

Assertion of the counter error output shall not, by itself, change the behavior of an in-progress reseed operation. The error indication is provided as status for use by higher-level error handling logic.
